quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hungarian is one of the few languages in the world that uses the unique letter 'ő' (o with double accents). When Hungarians answer the phone, they traditionally say 'Hallom' (I hear you) rather than 'hello.' The Hungarian language is also famous for having one of the longest words in the world: 'Megszentségteleníthetetlenségeskedéseitekért' with 44 letters!

short_read.title: The Secret Life of Garden Snails
short_read.teaser: Those little snails in your garden are more remarkable than you might think—they have thousands of tiny teeth and can sleep for three years! Discover the surprising world of these patient garden companions.

medium_read.title: How Hummingbirds Became Nature's Helicopters
medium_read.teaser: Hummingbirds can fly backwards, hover in place, and beat their wings up to 80 times per second. Scientists have discovered the incredible evolutionary journey that gave these tiny birds their amazing aerial abilities.

long_read.title: The Women Who Mapped the Ocean Floor
long_read.teaser: Marie Tharp's revolutionary maps revealed underwater mountains and valleys no one knew existed, changing our understanding of Earth forever. Her story is one of perseverance, scientific brilliance, and seeing what others couldn't imagine.

port_angeles.title: Eagles Over the Strait
port_angeles.description: August is a wonderful time to spot bald eagles along the Strait of Juan de Fuca as they hunt for salmon. The Ediz Hook area and Dungeness Spit are particularly good viewing spots where you can often see these magnificent birds soaring overhead or perched in shoreline trees.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart can beat up to ___ times per minute during flight.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Amazing! You're absolutely right—1,200 beats per minute! That tiny heart works incredibly hard to power those amazing wings.
puzzle_1.close_response: You're so close! The actual number is 1,200 beats per minute—that's about 20 times faster than a human heart!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: That tiny hummingbird heart actually beats an incredible 1,200 times per minute during flight—about 20 times faster than ours!
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: To fuel this incredible heart rate, hummingbirds must eat about half their body weight in sugar every day and visit hundreds of flowers. They have the highest metabolism of any animal on Earth.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderful! Pillangó is indeed butterfly—such a lovely, lilting word for such a delicate creature!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The Hungarian word for butterfly is 'pillangó'—doesn't it sound just as graceful as the creature itself? (Virág means flower, madár means bird, and napsugár means sunbeam.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Many Hungarian words are beautifully descriptive. 'Pillangó' may come from an old word meaning 'fluttering one,' perfectly capturing the butterfly's gentle flight through summer gardens.

puzzle_3.question: What do scientists call the study of birds?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Perfect! Ornithology is the study of birds, from the Greek word 'ornis' meaning bird. The Olympic Peninsula is a wonderful place for bird watching!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: The study of birds is called ornithology, from the Greek word 'ornis.' Entomology studies insects, herpetology studies reptiles, and ichthyology studies fish—all fascinating fields!
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: The Olympic Peninsula is home to over 300 bird species, making it a paradise for ornithologists and bird lovers alike. From eagles to sandpipers, the variety of habitats supports an amazing diversity of birdlife.
puzzle_3.learn_more_label: Birds of Olympic National Park — NPS
